thread:
Maria Ramos: heads-up — we just started seeing a sustained p95/p99 latency spike on hosted API /v1/generate in us-east-1. queue depth is steadily growing, errors for timeouts rising. happening across multiple models (gpt-3.8-small and gpt-4-xxr)

Ops Bot: INCIDENT ALERT: hosted-api:queue_growth_us-east-1 at 2026-03-15T18:07:14Z — paging SRE Oncall

SRE Oncall: I’m on pager. pulling logs now. initial look: backlog up from ~200 to ~3.2k in last 12m, provisioner failing to create nodes (rate limited by cloud API). autoscaler logs show repeated ProvisionerRateLimit errors.

Liam Chen: confirmed from telemetry — GPU pool us-east-1a at 98% alloc, attempts to spin ups are hitting account-level VM quota. also seeing a handful of oversized jobs from a partner partner-acme that are saturating KV caches.

Eva Park: customers complaining via support channel — multiple teams reporting 502/504, increased retry loops. Support Bot forwarded some of the customer messages.

Support Bot: 3 high-sev customer complaints in last 8m: "generation timed out", "requests stuck for >30s", one reported user-facing error in production.

Samir Gupta: quick mitigation idea: enable emergency fallback routing to the lighter-weight quantized variants and enable prefix caching for repeated queries. we can also apply per-customer throttles for non-enterprise plans.

Priya Nair (Eng Lead): agree. need to coordinate infra to request quota bump and also run temporary admission controls so we don't starve enterprise reserved pools. Liaise with cloud-ops.

SRE Oncall: rolling list of actions, stepwise: 1) enable immediate routing fallback to model-quantized variants for non-SLA customers, 2) apply soft throttles (20%) on best-effort plans, 3) try manual scale-up of dedicated pools (if quota allows), 4) investigate provisioner rate-limit error path. executing 1+2 now.

Liam Chen: pushing a route change now — temp-route rule: if customer_tier != "enterprise" then route to quantized-compat model. command: ```reconfigure-router --region us-east-1 --condition 'customer_tier!=enterprise' --target quantized-compat```

SRE Oncall: applied soft throttles via admission controller for 'best-effort' plans. throttle rule: 0.8 concurrency quota. Added reject-with-503 for burst above threshold. watch for broken clients.

Maria Ramos: adding a note for observability: set a temporary dashboard with these panels: queue depth, provisioner errors, p95/p99 for region, per-tenant error rate. also start a rolling 1m Slack summary every 5m.

Ops Bot: ACTION LOGGED: routing rollback and throttle changes made by SRE Oncall. Creating incident timeline entry.

Liam Chen: infra side — requested quota increase from cloud console but cloud support is slow tonight. opened a request (REQ-9342). fallback plan: spin up smaller instances type (g4dn->g5.xsmall?) to satisfy capacity quickly, but performance hit.

Samir Gupta: enable per-tenant token-bucket policing for customers with heavy short-lived bursts. config snippet below: ```rate_limit: {burst_tokens: 500, refill_rate_per_s: 50,policy: best_effort_drop}```

Eva Park: support is triaging customers. escalation notes: mark enterprise customers as priority (no throttles), notify any with active SLAs. Laura from Acme flagged that their batch job is running now and they are on paid plan.

Priya Nair (Eng Lead): @Maria can you take customer-impact summary for PG and Acme? Need to call CS and give ETA. I'll lead the engineering coordination.

Maria Ramos: on it. early estimate: ~12 tenants affected with visible 5xx spikes; roughly 7% of hosted traffic in the region impacted, concentrated on high-concurrency endpoints. I’ll call CS to notify top 3 enterprise customers and offer guidance. ETA for visible improvements after routing fallback: 3-6 minutes (observed reductions in queue within 2m for small-scale tests).

SRE Oncall: queue depth down from 3.2k -> 1.1k after fallback + throttles. p95 dropped from 2.4s -> 1.1s, p99 still high at 4.8s. timeouts reduced but not eliminated. provisioner still showing rate-limit errors on node creation attempts.

Liam Chen: created a temporary dedicated pool with smaller instances (type g5.xlarge) that our quota permits. spun up 6 nodes; should add ~200 concurrent slots. logs show they joined runtime.

Ops Bot: DEPLOYMENT EVENT: temporary-pool-us-east-2026-03-15 created by Liam Chen at 18:16:42Z.

Samir Gupta: recommending to enable KV prefix cache hotpath for top 20 hot prefixes — that cuts per-token work for repeated completions. can push config change: ```cache.hot_prefixes = top20; cache.ttl = 600s```

SRE Oncall: applied first 2 hot prefixes. monitoring CPU/GPU utilization — small win on p99.

Eva Park: update from support — two enterprise customers reported transient errors but all non-blocking; they asked for ETA and mitigation steps we’re taking. I gave them a 30m ETA for stable behavior.

Priya Nair (Eng Lead): we need a short-term post-incident action: 1) increase cloud API quota for account 2) improve provisioner backoff to avoid rate-limit thrashing 3) add per-tenant tail-protection 4) run a test so that partner-acme's batch jobs are scheduled more fairly. assigning tasks after handoff.

Maria Ramos: I'm scheduling the CS+Account call now for top affected customers; will send the incident summary doc in 15m and keep them updated.

SRE Oncall: final state at 18:26Z: backlog down to ~420, p95=0.9s, p99=2.2s, error rate trending down. provisioner requests still showing occasional 429 from cloud API but retry spacing is working so growth is controlled. moving to monitoring mode.

Liam Chen: cloud support pushed partial quota emergency increase (temp +10 vCPUs) — should help with more medium nodes if needed. open ticket REF-7321.

Priya Nair (Eng Lead): great. preparing handoff to night SRE in 20m. Drafting short summary for oncall: cause = bursty partner job + quota-limited autoscaler causing lag, mitigations = fallback routing + throttles + temp small-instance pool + hot-prefix caching, customer impact = ~12 tenants, 7% traffic, transient 5xx, current state = degrading to stable.

SRE Oncall: handoff note: I will update runbook with exact commands used for routing and throttles. leaving monitoring checks to next oncall. tagging @SRE-Oncall-Night.

Ops Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity reduced to SEV-2. Handoff scheduled at 18:45Z.

Maria Ramos: customer impact summary posted to incident doc and pinged CS leads. will follow-up with postmortem action items after incident is closed.

Samir Gupta: follow-up tasks that I have captured: 1) automated detection of provisioner rate-limit surge 2) circuit breaker that demotes non-enterprise traffic earlier 3) infra quota runbook for emergency request 4) KV cache autoscale for hot prefixes.

Priya Nair (Eng Lead): assigning tasks in GH. thanks team — nice quick coordination.

SRE Oncall: closing active mitigation. monitoring for 30m then will transition to postmortem. please add any outstanding notes to the incident timeline. :thumbsup:
